analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: AI & Semis in focus; Q3 reporting kicks off AMSL, TSCM, PUB; Inwit press; Cutting Prosus estimates; NVidia & Reflection; 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: The week centres on AI/semis: SEMICON West and the OCP Global Summit give updates on advanced-packaging bottlenecks, power, cooling and networking. Earnings from ASML, TSMC, Publicis and Havas, plus capital markets days from Accenture and AMAT.

ASML reportedly raises prices on all EUV and DUV spare parts in Korea by 10%, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix accepting for deliveries from January 2027 (unconfirmed). Services, parts and upgrades were around 25% of 2025 revenue and are expected to grow by more than 30% in 2026. It is a modest cost headwind for the two Korean memory makers.

ASML results are Wednesday. Sell-side is broadly bullish and expects a solid quarter, potentially ahead of guidance. Buy-side sentiment is more mixed, flows are two-way, and some US hedge funds use ASML as a funding short. Positioning is better than last quarter.

ASML FY27 low-NA EUV capacity guidance is roughly 85 tools (buy-side closer to 90), with potential capacity of more than 110 tools by 2028. ASML broke ground on the BIC North campus near Eindhoven on 8 September, with the first phase due in 2029.

TSMC: Q3 revenue should be strong and a further Q4 raise is possible. The key debate is whether management gives visibility on 2027 capex. GIR raised its 2027E/2028E capex forecasts to US$85bn/US$98bn from US$78bn/US$82bn.

Publicis Q3: GIR expects organic growth of 4.8%, in line with consensus, while the buy-side hurdle is above 5%. Q3 is a revenue-only update. Q4 guidance is likely around 4-5%. Key questions are the 2027 LiveRamp and free-cash-flow outlook and the scale of weakness at Sapient. Positioning is less extreme than in past quarters.

USITC opened a preliminary Section 337 patent investigation into Vicor's vertical power-delivery technology, naming 20 companies including Infineon. It is expected to take 12-18 months. Near-term risks are legal costs, hyperscaler qualification hesitancy and licence pressure. An industry-wide settlement or licensing framework is the most likely outcome.

Nvidia is reportedly in early talks (FT) to acquire Reflection AI, last valued around $25bn, or expand its ~$800m stake, possibly through an acqui-hire or licensing structure to ease regulatory scrutiny. Motivation is custom ASIC adoption by hyperscalers and frontier labs, and the wish to offer US open-weight alternatives to Chinese models.
Amazon is reportedly in talks to buy Decart AI for around $7bn, after Anthropic previously considered a roughly $6bn purchase and did not proceed.

Prosus/Naspers 1H27 preview: FY27/28 EPS estimates cut by 7%/9%, 5%/9% below consensus. 1H27 adjusted EBITDA forecast at $362m, 22% below consensus, ahead of results on 24 November. Discount to NAV widened to 39% versus a 38% long-term average. Prosus target rises to EUR40 from EUR39 and Naspers target falls to ZAR863 from ZAR864, both Neutral.

INWIT's main shareholders (Ardian 32%, KKR-backed Oak Holdings 1 at 39%) are reportedly arranging financing to buy the remaining 29% free float, with Mubadala in talks to join. Shares are down about 27% over the past year, with a market value of about EUR6.3bn, amid lease disputes with TIM and Fastweb.

Memory and hardware pricing: Taiwan OSAT price hikes of up to 30%, AMD GPU prices up around 10%, Nvidia RTX 50-series prices in Germany up to 66% higher versus up to 46% for AMD. Samsung reportedly plans to cut 4Q smartphone output by 20-30%. Smartphone DRAM prices reportedly rose 175% y/y to US$145-146 in 3Q, with a further ~20% q/q increase expected in 4Q.
Apple reportedly cut iPhone 18 Pro component orders by up to 15% and raised Pro Max orders by 10-15%, leaving Pro-series volume broadly unchanged.
China's CXMT, with around 10% of global DRAM revenue, claims progress on a 4F² DRAM design and aims to launch a server-memory product by end-2026. Samsung and SK Hynix are at the planning stage.
GS raised its year-end 2026 US data center capacity forecast by 5 GW to 64 GW and cut year-end 2027 by 5 GW to 90 GW. The ERCOT 2027 forecast is down 1 GW on stricter interconnection requirements.
Lumentum says optical component capacity is effectively sold out into early 2029, with revenue potentially doubling y/y in 2026 and at least US$350mn of Tokyo-area capacity investment planned.
Inference-economy software names (SNOW, CRWD, PANW, NET, PLTR) are at or near all-time highs even as semis stumbled. Investors question whether numbers will rise enough to support the multiples.

SpaceX and European telcos: investors see the US as SpaceX's priority given ARPU of roughly EUR40-44 a month versus EUR14-15 in the EU. The overhang may persist, with the UK via Vodafone's MVNO a possible cheap entry. Polymarket prices 26% for a SpaceX US mobile plan by June 2027 and 43% by end-2027.
Telia is cutting around 900 roles, targeting SEK 1bn of annual gross savings, with about SEK 600m of restructuring charges in Q4 2026. Full run-rate is expected by 2028.

US prime brokerage data: fundamental long/short managers down 0.2% on the week and up 12.5% YTD, systematic up 0.1% and up 20.8% YTD. The global book was net sold, led by EM and North America. Europe was net bought for a fourth week. Info Tech and Communication Services were the most net sold sectors.
Google is reportedly testing Carbon, potentially competitive with Opus 5.5. Polymarket prices Google as a serious contender for best model by year end.

market_movers.rationale: Reported 10% Korean spare-parts price increase supports services growth and margins ahead of Wednesday's results. Expectations remain high.
Q3 revenue looks strong and a Q4 raise is possible. The debate is 2027 capex visibility.
Publicis Q3 organic growth expected at 4.8%, in line with consensus. Buy-side hurdle is above 5%.
Named in a USITC Section 337 investigation into Vicor's patents. Risks are legal costs and customer qualification hesitancy.
Target raised to EUR40 from EUR39 while FY27/28 EPS estimates were cut 7%/9% on food-delivery investment, lower Tencent forecasts and higher interest costs.
Naspers target trimmed to ZAR863 from ZAR864.
Optical component capacity is reportedly sold out into early 2029 on AI datacenter demand.
Reportedly in early talks to acquire Reflection AI or expand its stake, moving closer to frontier-model development.

sector_views.rationale: AI demand is driving pricing power and sold-out capacity across equipment, packaging, optical and memory, although Korean memory names face cost and China competition pressure.
European telcos face a SpaceX overhang and INWIT tenant disputes, while Telia cuts costs.

earnings_insights: ASML Q3 results Wednesday: sell-side expects a solid quarter potentially ahead of guidance. Buy-side sentiment is mixed.
TSMC Q3 (estimate, GS preview): revenue looks strong with a possible further Q4 guidance raise. GIR 2027E/2028E capex forecast US$85bn/US$98bn versus US$78bn/US$82bn previously.
Publicis Q3 (estimate): GIR expects organic growth of 4.8%, broadly in line with consensus. The buy-side hurdle is above 5%. Revenue-only update with no margin disclosure.
Prosus 1H27 (estimate, results 24 November): adjusted EBITDA of $362m forecast by GS, 22% below consensus. FY27/28 EPS estimates cut 7%/9%, 5%/9% below consensus.
Worldline 3Q26 results scheduled 27 October: GS lowers FY26 financial services organic growth to -6.6% from -6%, with total FY26E organic revenue growth broadly unchanged at about 0%.
risk_factors: ASML expectations remain high and the Korean price increase is unconfirmed.
TSMC may offer no 2027 capex visibility.
Publicis: tough Q4 comparatives, uncertain budget flush and the macro backdrop. Sapient weakness is a significant headwind.
Infineon: legal costs, hyperscaler qualification hesitancy and licensing pressure from the Vicor investigation.
Memory cost inflation is cutting smartphone production and straining Korean memory makers, with Chinese competition from CXMT.
Inference-economy software multiples depend on numbers rising enough.
Political scrutiny and stricter interconnection requirements may constrain US data center growth.
INWIT lease disputes with TIM and Fastweb.
vol_and_positioning: Last week's prime brokerage top 10 week-on-week increases in GS shorts by market value included three TMT names: BESI, IFX and PUB.
Some US hedge funds are using ASML as a funding short, and flows are two-way. Positioning is better than last quarter.
Publicis positioning is less extreme than in past quarters, with a fair few investors on the fence.
Fundamental long/short managers are down 0.2% on the week and up 12.5% YTD. Systematic managers are up 0.1% on the week and up 20.8% YTD.
geopolitical: US-China competition in memory, with CXMT advancing a 4F² DRAM design.
Chinese low-cost AI models such as DeepSeek cited as a driver of Nvidia's interest in US open-weight alternatives.

tension_points.bull_case: Sell-side expects a solid quarter potentially ahead of guidance on stronger memory and logic system sales, improving margins and spare-parts pricing power.
tension_points.bear_case: Buy-side sentiment is mixed, flows are two-way with more selling, and some hedge funds use ASML as a funding short. Expectations remain high.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 could beat on the day, with account wins, a c.200bp new-business tailwind and less extreme positioning.
tension_points.bear_case: Expected in-line results and cautious Q4 guidance of about 4-5% make it hard to hold gains, and Sapient is a significant headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Organic growth below the 4.8% GS expects, or a weak 2027 LiveRamp and free-cash-flow outlook.
